title: Incremental record resolution
summary: Reuse the unchanged Cinderline resolver as a byte-identical reference and apply it to a second plant's raw deliveries: duplicates, late older revisions, valid corrections, conflicting payloads and unkeyed conflicts.
outcome: Predict accepted state, totals, quarantine and the publication decision for changing records, and explain why replay never inflates accepted totals.
environment: Python 3.12 standard library; the reference resolver is pure Python and is hash-checked against the original package.
evidence: 24 tests executed locally with zero skips; fixture and output hashes and the reference SHA-256 are recorded in docs/academy/labs/lab-l06-record-resolution.json.
downloadDescription: Original resolver reference (unchanged, hash-checked) with a second-plant transfer fixture, authored expected states, starters, solutions and tests. Python 3.12, no Spark.

title: Data contracts and quarantine
summary: Validate schema, keys, quantities and cross-record constraints over synthetic inspection deliveries, quarantine rows with reasons, and show why row-level checks cannot establish uniqueness or completeness on their own.
outcome: Write a contract-driven validator, read a quarantine by reason, and separate row-level validity from multi-row and source-completeness evidence.
evidence: 19 tests executed locally with zero skips, including a permissive validator that fails for the asserted reason; hashes in docs/academy/labs/lab-l10-contracts-quarantine.json.
downloadDescription: Contract validator lab: fixtures, expected quarantine with reasons, manifest-count transfer case, starters, solutions and tests. Python 3.12, no Spark.

title: SQL and PySpark equivalence
summary: The same typed synthetic inspection data transformed with Spark SQL and with the DataFrame API; results and types are compared deliberately, including an order-dependent failure and null-handling divergences until corrected.
outcome: Write the same transformation both ways, compare schemas and sorted rows, and explain why implicit row order and null comparisons break equivalence.
environment: Python 3.12, Apache Spark 4.0.4 (PySpark, local[2], UI off), Java 21.
evidence: 9 tests executed locally with zero skips; fixture and output hashes in docs/academy/labs/lab-l02-sql-pyspark-equivalence.json.
downloadDescription: Equivalence lab: fixtures, authored expected rows, SQL and DataFrame starters, solutions and tests. Local Spark 4.0.4, no cloud.

title: Join cardinality and weighted metrics
summary: A plausible incorrect total from a multiplying join, its diagnosis by counts and duplicate keys, the repair, a weighted-rate versus average-of-rates trap, a left-join count trap and a transfer test on a different duplicated dimension.
outcome: Detect and repair a multiplying join, compute a weighted metric correctly and read a null-propagating count.
environment: Python 3.12, Apache Spark 4.0.4 (PySpark, local[2], UI off), Java 21.
evidence: 9 tests executed locally with zero skips; hashes in docs/academy/labs/lab-l03-join-cardinality.json.
downloadDescription: Join-cardinality lab: fixtures with duplicated dimension rows, authored expected totals, starters, solutions and tests. Local Spark 4.0.4, no cloud.

title: Point-in-time features
summary: Build a feature table from timestamped sensor readings whose two-hour windows publish thirty minutes after they close, join it to labelled prediction times as of what was actually known, and prove that future readings, duplicate entity-time rows and a drifted serving transform are all rejected.
outcome: Construct a point-in-time-correct training set, name the leak in event-time and latest-value shortcuts, catch training/serving skew with a consistency check, and explain which predictions change when late readings append new feature versions.
environment: Python 3.12 with pandas 3.0.6 and numpy 2.5.3; no Spark, Java, MLflow or network.
evidence: 25 tests executed locally with zero skips, including shortcut starters that fail for their documented reason; hashes in docs/academy/labs/lab-l18-point-in-time-features.json.
downloadDescription: Point-in-time feature lab: timestamped readings, late arrivals, labels, a feature contract, authored expected tables, starters with deliberate shortcuts, a reference solution and tests. Python 3.12 with pandas; no Spark.

title: Transactional state for a quality-review app
summary: Constraints, an idempotent at-least-once intake, a work queue claimed with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED across two real sessions, optimistic concurrency with a version column, isolation timelines and a least-privilege application role, all on a local PostgreSQL 16 server, plus a Lakebase adaptation guide kept separate from what ran.
outcome: Design operational state that survives redelivery and concurrent reviewers, show why an unlocked read-then-update double-claims and last-write-wins loses a decision, and list what a managed Lakebase deployment would still need to prove.
environment: Python 3.12 standard library driving a throwaway local PostgreSQL 16 server (initdb, pg_ctl, psql) on 127.0.0.1; managed Lakebase, OAuth, the pooler and synced tables were not executed.
evidence: 18 tests executed locally against PostgreSQL 16.13 with zero skips; ten Lakebase platform steps are listed as not executed in docs/academy/labs/lab-l23-transactional-state.json.
downloadDescription: Transactional-state lab: schema, grants, claim, decision and intake SQL with starters, fixtures, hand-derived expected results, a local PostgreSQL 16 test harness and a Lakebase adaptation guide. Requires PostgreSQL 16 server tools; no Databricks workspace.

title: Plans, shuffles and skew
summary: Read the plans Spark prints for a narrow chain, a grouped sum, a sort-merge and a broadcast join, a window, a salted join and a cached filter over a 240-row synthetic feed, predict each expensive boundary, then compare the prediction with the jobs, stages, tasks and shuffle records Spark actually executed, including adaptive coalescing, a runtime join switch and skew splitting.
outcome: Locate exchanges and stage boundaries in an explained plan, explain why a hot key never splits by repartitioning, show that salting spreads it while keeping totals, and tell a plan change from an answer change.
environment: Python 3.12, Apache Spark 4.0.4 (PySpark, local[2], UI off, four shuffle partitions), Java 21; shuffle records read from Spark's status store. No timings are measured.
evidence: 14 tests executed locally with zero skips; expected values come from a plain-Python derivation that never imports Spark. Hashes and the recorded adaptive build sides are in docs/academy/labs/lab-l04-plans-shuffle.json.
downloadDescription: Execution-evidence lab: seeded skewed and balanced inspection feeds, an independent expected-value derivation, starter and solution evidence functions and tests. Local Spark 4.0.4, no cloud.

title: Python parsing under a contract
summary: Turn a CSV delivery and a JSON delivery from two fictional plants into typed Python values under one small contract, or reject each record with a named reason and its raw input, so that accepted plus rejected equals received; a third plant's transfer delivery breaks the same rules in new ways.
outcome: Parse and validate records with explicit types, tell null from missing from blank from zero, keep rejections with reasons, log without side effects at import, and prove each rule with a test that fails for the stated defect.
environment: Python 3.12 standard library only; nothing to install.
evidence: 36 tests executed locally with zero skips; a shipped mutation check shows fourteen one-line defects each failing a test. Hashes in docs/academy/labs/lab-l01-python-parsing.json.
downloadDescription: Parsing lab: CSV and JSON deliveries, a transfer delivery, authored expected results, a naive and a starter parser, a reference solution, tests and a mutation check. Python 3.12 standard library.

title: Time-aware analytical SQL
summary: A Spark SQL portfolio over five synthetic plant files: window frames, ranking and deduplication, gaps and islands, membership with EXISTS versus IN and NULLs, set operations, nested fields, safe casts under ANSI mode and daylight-saving-time arithmetic, with every expected value written down before the query ran.
outcome: Predict a window's rows and a query's result row by row, choose the membership form that survives NULLs, cast defensively, and state which time zone a timestamp calculation used.
environment: Python 3.12, Apache Spark 4.0.4 (PySpark, local[2], UI off, ANSI mode on, session time zone America/New_York), Java 21.
evidence: 51 tests executed locally with zero skips; time-zone answers come from an independent zoneinfo script that never touches Spark. Hashes in docs/academy/labs/lab-l12-time-aware-sql.json.
downloadDescription: Analytical SQL lab: five synthetic fixtures, hand-derived and independently derived expected results, a starter and a reference SQL portfolio, and tests. Local Spark 4.0.4, no cloud.
